function: Joint learning of spatial-frequency user scheduling, hybrid (analog and baseband) precoding and analog combining in downlink wideband MU-MIMO OFDM, maximizing spectral efficiency (p. 1, 4-5).
system: Downlink MU-MIMO OFDM at 28 GHz, 400 MHz: BS with 8-128 antennas and 2-12 RF chains, 1-60 candidate users with 1-8 antennas each; no RIS (p. 4, 11).
method: Two cascaded GNNs (scheduler: 3D-GNN or sequence of GNNs; precoder: 3D-GNN with partial attention), unsupervised on negative spectral efficiency; precoder pre-trained, then joint fine-tuning (p. 6-10).
data_channel: Simulated 3GPP TR 38.901 UMa NLOS channels with Table III parameters, CDL-A for the crowded-user case; 200,000 training and 2,000 test samples (p. 11-13, 16).
test_conditions: Each of RBs, users, BS antennas, user antennas varied separately: trained at 16, 30, 16, 4; tested without retraining on 4-128, 3-60, 8-128, 1-8 (p. 13).
baselines: Non-learned: LISA, Greedy, SDR, SVD, EIG, MO, OMP, LISA-SDR; learned: GAT, CNN, FNN scheduler-precoder pairs (p. 12).
metrics: Spectral efficiency and SE ratio to LISA-SDR; inference runtime, FLOPs order, trainable weights; training samples, training time (p. 12-14).
complexity: FLOPs orders (Table II); inference runtime 81-179 ms (NGNN, SGNN) vs 8927-9205 ms (LISA-SDR) and 635-662k weights (Table IV); training cost (Table V) (p. 11, 14).
q1_support: p. 11: "Consider a non-line-of-sight channel model in urban macro (UMa) scenario [35]"; p. 13: "clustered delay line-A model [35]"; p. 16: "3GPP, Study on Channel Model for Frequencies From 0.5 to 100 GHz, document TR 38.901"
q2_support: p. 13: "trained with samples of 16 RBs and tested with samples of 4 to 128 RBs without retraining"; the same is done for users, BS antennas and user antennas (p. 13).
q3_support: p. 12: "by comparing with three numerical algorithms for wideband scheduling and hybrid precoding: LISA [5], Greedy [6], and SDR [7]"; p. 12: "GAT: All 3D-GNNs in the SGNN are replaced by GATs"; p. 12: "CNN: Two CNNs, each composed of convolutional layers"; p. 12: "FNN: Two FNNs serve as the scheduler and precoder modules". SE compared in Figs. 6-7.
q4_support: p. 11: "The computational complexity for inference is measured in floating point operations (FLOPs)"; p. 14: "the time complexity refers to the runtime for inference, the space complexity refers to the number of trainable weights"
notes: The scheduler (above the physical layer) is learned jointly with hybrid precoding and analog combining (physical layer), so the work passes above_phy; area 3. q1 rests on reference [35] being 3GPP TR 38.901 (p. 16) for the UMa NLOS and CDL-A models; the main text cites it only as [35]. q5: the footnote says Data is available, with a GitHub link; reviewer to confirm what the repository holds. Journal extension of a WCNC 2024 paper (p. 1).
